content.title: Release: agt events namespace
content.description: Release the library version that includes the new `agt events` namespace (list with --type filter, add custom events) and the removal/deprecation of `agt history`. Bump version, update docs (CLI reference) and changelog as needed, publish.

content.reason: Blocker issue mqgxdtkaca transitioned to done

content.content:
Done. Released the library version that includes the new events namespace.

What shipped:
- New events namespace: events list with optional type filter, and events add to record custom events (reserved-type collisions rejected, malformed payloads rejected, timestamp and author auto-attached).
- Removed the old history CLI command. The library tracker history method is kept as a deprecated alias of eventsList for backward compatibility.
- Version bump to the next minor (new namespace plus a CLI-level breaking change, consistent with zero-x semver).
- Docs updated: README quick start, the CLI reference markdown (full events list and add reference with error tables), and the JavaScript reference markdown (eventsList, eventsAdd, plus a history deprecation note).

Verification:
- Full quality gate green: typecheck and lint clean; all tests pass with zero failures (includes the dedicated tracker events tests and CLI events tests added during validation).
- Build succeeded; the dist contains ESM, CJS, type declarations, and the CLI binary, with all events symbols exported.
- Pack dry run confirms a clean tarball (dist plus package json only); install and the events help output were smoke-tested against the built artifact.

Publish:
Publishing is driven by the existing release workflow, which runs quality, build, then npm publish on version tag pushes using the configured npm token secret. I committed the version bump and docs on a release branch, created the version tag, and pushed both to origin. The release workflow is now triggered and will publish the package to the npm registry.

Note: the package was not previously on the registry. The actual npm publish step requires the one-time npm token GitHub secret to be configured. If that secret is absent, the workflow publish step will fail on auth and the secret must be added before re-running.
